key_insight: Machine-learning-accelerated simulations reveal that surface polarons on reduced rutile TiO2(110) move far more slowly than in the bulk because surface hopping pathways are strongly restricted.
engineering_relevance: This explains why porous rutile TiO2 can show much lower electron mobility than single-crystal material, which matters for catalysis, photovoltaics, batteries, and energy-storage devices.
method: Extended a machine-learning-assisted polaron dynamics approach to an oxide surface.
Simulated oxygen-deficient rutile TiO2(110) for several nanoseconds across multiple temperatures.
Analyzed polaron hopping pathways, interlayer events, and vacancy-induced charge localization.
evidence_signal: Several nanoseconds of temperature-dependent dynamics show surface small-polaron mobility suppressed by orders of magnitude relative to bulk, with rare interlayer hopping and vacancy-attracted charge localization.
watch_item: The findings are demonstrated for a specific reduced oxide surface, so transfer to other oxides, defect densities, or surface terminations should be validated before device design use.
paper_title: Machine-learned dynamics of surface polarons at reduced oxide surfaces
